title: Opening and Funding a Certificate of Deposit
content:
A certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line opens in applied status at the rate and annual percentage yield fixed on the opening date, and it begins to run only when the opening deposit posts.

## 1. Admission of the applicant

The customer's age in whole years on the opening date, taken from the date of birth on the customer profile, must be at least the youngest age the tier publishes. The date of birth on the profile governs; an age the customer states does not.

## 2. The opening deposit

The opening deposit must be a single deposit of at least the tier's smallest opening deposit and at most the largest principal a certificate of the tier may hold, arriving by one of the sources the tier accepts. On a tier whose funds must be new to Piedmont Crescent Bank, an internal transfer from any Piedmont Crescent account is not accepted.

A deposit drawn from a Piedmont Crescent checking or savings account debits that account as the deposit posts, and that account must belong to the same customer.

## 3. Funding, the term start and the maturity date

The certificate is funded, and becomes active, on the business day the opening deposit posts. That date is the start of the term. The maturity date is the term start plus the number of months the tier publishes as its term, counted in calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist.

## 4. Lapse of a certificate never funded

A certificate still in applied status is closed as unfunded once the calendar days the tier publishes as its funding window have passed after the certificate was opened. Calendar days are counted with the day after the opening date as day 1, and the lapse is due when the current date is on or after the opening date plus the funding window. The opening date is read from the certificate record.

### Boundary readings, on hypothetical dates

A certificate of a tier whose funding window is 10 days is opened on 4 March and is still unfunded.

| Current date | Opening date plus the window | Is the lapse due |
|---|---|---|
| 13 March | 14 March | no; the date is before it |
| 14 March | 14 March | yes; the date is on it, and the boundary day itself counts |
| 15 March | 14 March | yes |

A term of 6 months beginning on 31 August matures on 28 February, or on 29 February in a leap year, because no 31 February exists and the count falls back to the last day of that month.
